'''Minor Jesser Coon''' (July 29, 1921 – September 5, 2018)<ref name="obit" /> was an American [[biochemist]] and Victor V Vaughan Distinguished University Professor [[Emeritus]] at the [[University of Michigan, Ann Arbor]].<ref name=umich>{{cite web|title=Minor Coon, Ph.D.|url=https://medicine.umich.edu/dept/biochem/minor-coon-phd|website=University of Michigan, Ann Arbor|access-date=12 January 2016}}</ref> He is best known for his research on [[cytochrome P-450]]<ref name=kresge>{{cite journal|last1=Kresge|first1=Nicole|last2=Simoni|first2=Robert D.|last3=Hill|first3=Robert L.|title=The Purification of Cytochrome P-450 and Its Isozymes: the Work of Minor J. Coon|journal=Journal of Biological Chemistry|year=2006|volume=281|issue=47|page=e38|doi=10.1016/S0021-9258(20)68201-1|url=http://www.jbc.org/content/281/47/e38#ref-1|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=sies>{{cite journal|last1=Sies|first1=Helmut|title=Tribute to Professor Minor J. Coon|journal=Archives of Biochemistry and Biophysics|date=March 2011|volume=507|issue=1|pages=3|doi=10.1016/j.abb.2011.01.025|pmid=21324388}}</ref><ref name=porter>{{cite journal|last1=Porter|first1=T. D.|title=Jud Coon: 35 Years of P450 Research, A Synopsis of P450 History|journal=Drug Metabolism and Disposition|date=1 January 2004|volume=32|issue=1|pages=1–6|doi=10.1124/dmd.32.1.1|pmid=14709613}}</ref> and as the co-discoverer of [[HMG-CoA]], along with [[Bimal Kumar Bachhawat]].<ref name="Classics in Indian Medicine">{{cite journal|url=http://www.nmji.in/archives/Volume-28/Issue-3/Classics-in-Indian-Medicine.pdf |title=Classics in Indian Medicine |author=Debi P. Sarkar |journal=The National Medical Journal of India |year=2015 |issue=28 |pages=3 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531082638/http://www.nmji.in/archives/Volume-28/Issue-3/Classics-in-Indian-Medicine.pdf |archive-date=2016-05-31}}</ref><ref name="An outstanding scientist and a splendid human being">{{cite journal | title=An outstanding scientist and a splendid human being | author=Avadhesha Surolia | author-link=Avadhesha Surolia | journal=Glycobiology | year=1997 | volume=7 | issue=4 | pages=v–ix | doi = 10.1093/glycob/7.4.453| doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Deceased Fellow">{{cite web | url=http://www.insaindia.org.in/deceaseddetail.php?id=N730036 | title=Deceased Fellow | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=May 15, 2016 | url-status=usurped | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160815224551/http://www.insaindia.org.in/deceaseddetail.php?id=N730036 | archive-date=August 15, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=World Who's who in Science: A Biographical Dictionary of Notable Scientists from Antiquity to the Present|last=Debus|first=Allen G.|publisher=Marquis-Who's Who|year=1968}}</ref> He died on September 5, 2018, from complications due to [[Alzheimer's disease]].<ref name="obit">{{Cite web|url=https://www.niefuneralhomes.com/obituaries/Minor-Coon/|title=Minor "Jud" Jesser Coon - View Obituary & Service Information|website=Minor "Jud" Jesser Coon Obituary|access-date=2018-09-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913185550/https://www.niefuneralhomes.com/obituaries/Minor-Coon/|archive-date=2018-09-13|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Coon was born in [[Englewood, Colorado]], in 1921. He was an [[undergraduate]] student at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] and received his [[bachelor's degree]] with honors in 1943.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://obits.mlive.com/obituaries/annarbor/obituary.aspx?n=minor-coon&pid=190230123|title=Coon Obituary|date=October 22, 2018|website=MLive|access-date=October 22, 2018}}</ref> He received his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1946, supervised by [[William Cumming Rose]]. During his graduate work he studied [[amino acid]] [[metabolism]] and [[nitrogen balance]] using himself and his fellow students as volunteer subjects.<ref name=kresge /><ref name=coon_jbc>{{cite journal|last1=Coon|first1=M. J.|title=Enzyme Ingenuity in Biological Oxidations: a Trail Leading to Cytochrome P450|journal=Journal of Biological Chemistry|date=5 June 2002|volume=277|issue=32|pages=28351–28363|doi=10.1074/jbc.R200015200|pmid=12050174|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Academic career==
After a year as a [[postdoctoral fellow]] at the University of Illinois, Coon became a faculty member at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1947. He moved to the [[University of Michigan Medical School]] in 1955 and remained there for the remainder of his career, chairing the biological chemistry department from 1970 to 1990 and becoming the Victor V. Vaughan Distinguished University Professor of Biological Chemistry in 1983. Coon served as the president of the [[American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology]] from 1991 to 1992.<ref name=kresge /> He became a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 1983 and a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1984. A biological chemistry professorship in his honor was established at the University of Michigan in 1991.<ref name=umich />

Coon mentored many graduate students and promoted teaching along with research, including [[David Ballou]] and Professor Emeritus [[Tetsufumi Ueda]], a pioneer in neuroscience.<ref name=biochemnews>{{cite web|url=https://medicine.umich.edu/sites/default/files/content/downloads/Newsletter2003.pdf|title=Department of Biological Chemistry Newsletter 2003|access-date=2018-12-13}}</ref><ref name=chemtree>{{cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=71702|title=Minor J. Coon PhD|access-date=2018-12-13}}</ref> The Minor J. and Mary Lou Coon Award was established by him and his wife, to recognize an outstanding graduate student in biological chemistry at the University of Michigan who excels at teaching, research, and service.

==Interests==
Coon was a patron of the arts.

==Awards and honors==
Coon has received a number of awards in recognition of his scientific achievements.<ref name=umich />
*[[Paul-Lewis Award in Enzyme Chemistry]], 1959
*[[William C. Rose Award]] in Biochemistry, 1978
*[[American Society for Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics#Awards|Bernard B. Brodie Award in Drug Metabolism]], 1980
*Member, [[United States National Academy of Sciences]], 1983
*Fellow, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], 1984
*Member, [[Institute of Medicine]], 1987
*Honorary Doctor of Medicine, [[Karolinska Institute]]
